verdict.rationale: Ubuntu's own documentation says Ubuntu Desktop is certified on the Raspberry Pi and delivers a rich developer experience there. Together with its general claim of supporting all major IDEs, this addresses the core of the story. It rests on a single marketing mention with no detail on performance, setup, or tooling on such boards. Missing for 10: documentation of other low-cost single-board computers beyond Raspberry Pi, installation and performance details for Arm boards, confirmation that the full IDE and toolchain set runs on Arm, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can get a full desktop developer experience running on low-cost single-board computers

citations.quote: Ubuntu Desktop is also certified on the Raspberry Pi, delivering a rich developer experience on this powerful Arm device.
Ubuntu is a primary platform for all major IDEs, game development tools, and AI/ML software.
